clauses.reason: The plugin carried the guard at the cost of host-specific updates, duplicate Skills and a second release change; the Skill folder with a host hook entry carries the same guard without them.

updates.rationale: The published release already carries the Skill archive, its source metadata and checksums, so reading it directly removes the marketplace pin and its second release change. Replacing the folder in place keeps every hook path stable, so no host re-reviews or reinstalls anything after an update.
updates.statement: Manifest format stays 5. Omitted evidence fields mean the published evidence protocol and schema digest, and an explicit digest must equal that schema. update resolves the newest published GitHub release of R0k1e/Signetum, downloads its Skill archive, release-source.json and SHA256SUMS, verifies both files against the checksums and the extracted Skill's version and content digest against the release metadata, prepares that candidate's environment and checks the project manifest, then replaces the installed Skill folder in place from a staged sibling copy, rolls back a failed swap and verifies the result. A Skill folder inside a Git work tree is refused; a checkout follows Git and setup. An equal Skill digest or an older release changes nothing, an incompatible manifest returns migration_required before replacement, and --check stays read-only. update runs no host command and never edits a project or hook configuration; a hook names the stable Skill path and survives an update. Skill content identity and engine implementation identity stay separate and share one labeled digest function.

updates.rationale: A path-independent fingerprint lets every installed copy and an update candidate share one prepared environment, and a Skill directory without generated files keeps the content digest that update and install verify.
updates.statement: The locked engine environment lives in ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/signetum/runtime/<fingerprint>, where the fingerprint covers the implementation digest, uv.lock and pyproject.toml and not the install path. A shared runtime/host-python link only starts the launcher, which verifies the environment for its own fingerprint. setup and ordinary commands write nothing into the Skill directory except interpreter bytecode caches.

updates.rationale: The plugin existed mainly because a hook could only ship inside one. Hosts read hook entries from their own configuration, and the Skill already carries the guard script, so one folder serves every tool; this removes the Codex hook re-review and cache deletion on every update, the duplicate Skill next to a plain copy and the marketplace that a local folder could not refresh.
updates.statement: Signetum is distributed as one standard Agent Skill folder, skills/signetum, published with each release as signetum-skill-<version>.zip. Copying or unpacking that folder into any agent tool's skills directory is a complete install, and every protocol operation works without the command guard: receipts and batch-deliver as the only operation that advances the delivery branch carry the protocol guarantees, and the guard adds early refusal of work-losing commands. A host loads one Signetum Skill. New and existing projects share one explicit local adoption path. Internal scaffold materials are not a second public product.

updates.rationale: One folder to copy works in every tool; the optional command only automates placement and hook registration, so skipping it loses early refusal and nothing else.
updates.statement: Keep installation, distribution and use simple: one standard Skill folder for every agent tool, an optional deterministic install command that places it and registers the guard where a host reads hooks, and repository-owned instructions and commands. Position for reliable development with large agent teams using concrete cases and accurately bounded evidence.

updates.rationale: A user-level hook reaches every repository, so the adopted-repository check replaces the per-project plugin enablement that used to bound it without committing machine-specific hook paths into projects. Failing open keeps a broken guard from stopping every shell command; the owner accepted that trade.
updates.statement: The guard is an optional PreToolUse Bash hook entry in a host's configuration that runs an installed Skill's scripts/command-guard. It applies the whole rule set when the payload cwd lies in a Git work tree whose root holds signetum.toml and allows every command elsewhere. A missing interpreter, malformed payload, exception or timeout exits 0 with a diagnostic, and the sh entry maps every status other than 2 to 0. It prevents mistakes and is not a security boundary.

clauses.reason: There is no plugin to enable; install registers the guard per host and signetum.toml bounds where it applies.

updates.rationale: Project settings are committed with the repository, so every collaborator's host enables the guard there, and the guard's scope follows the repositories that adopted the protocol. Codex merges trusted project config layers into the plugin set, verified with codex-cli 0.166.0 in a temporary home.
updates.statement: The adoption preview that writes signetum.toml also enables the plugin at project scope: enabledPlugins signetum@signetum and the signetum GitHub marketplace in .claude/settings.json, and [plugins."signetum@signetum"] enabled = true in .codex/config.toml. Other settings are preserved, enabled files stay unchanged and an explicit disable is refused for review. Codex reads that layer only for trusted projects and only for a plugin installed in the user's Codex home.

clauses.reason: Record the optional install command, the guidance when the guard is absent and the tag-only release before implementation.

updates.rationale: A deterministic, previewable and reversible command replaces the plugin manager for the one thing the plugin added, the hook entry; placing the Skill and registering the hook together keeps the path the hook names correct. Removing an earlier user-scope plugin in the same step avoids two Skills, while project settings stay under the project's own review. Project-scope hook entries were not chosen because they would commit one machine's Skill path into the project.
updates.statement: sh <skill>/scripts/signetum install places the Skill at each target: --host claude at ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}/skills/signetum, --host codex at ${CODEX_HOME:-~/.codex}/skills/signetum, and --skills-dir DIR at DIR/signetum for any other tool. The source is the running Skill by default, a local Skill folder or release archive with --source, or a published release with --release <tag> or latest, verified like update. For each host target it writes one PreToolUse Bash entry running that copy's scripts/command-guard into the host's user hook configuration, settings.json for Claude Code and hooks.json for Codex, preserving every other setting and replacing only Signetum guard entries. It is idempotent; --preview reports the exact plan and writes nothing; --remove deletes the Signetum guard entries and the placed Skill. It refuses a target folder that is not a Signetum Skill or lies inside a Git work tree and never edits a project. When a host target also has the signetum@signetum plugin installed at user scope, install removes it through that host's plugin manager after the Skill and hook are in place, and reports a project-scope plugin with its removal command instead of running it.

updates.rationale: Without a plugin nothing enables the guard implicitly, so the one command an agent runs first states how to enable it; tying detection to the Skill's own location keeps it deterministic, and tools without a known hook surface are not nagged.
updates.statement: When the running Skill sits in a Claude Code or Codex user skills directory and no hook entry in that host's user configuration or in the project's .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json or .codex/hooks.json runs its scripts/command-guard, status reports one guard entry naming the host, the install command and the exact hook entry to add by hand. The guidance never blocks or changes an operation, and a Skill anywhere else reports nothing about the guard.

updates.rationale: A pin recording the release commit cannot be part of that commit, so it forced a second change after every release; the published release already binds the exact source and checksums.
updates.statement: A release is one delivered change that sets the product version and its notes, followed by an annotated v<version> tag on the delivered main commit; the release workflow publishes the Skill archive, internal wheel and sdist, release-source.json, release notes and SHA256SUMS. No file on main records a release, and update and install --release read published releases.

decisions.reason: The owner reopened plugin distribution: the Skill folder becomes the unit of distribution, an optional install command registers the guard in each host's own hook configuration, and a release is its tag alone.

boundaries: One manifest format and one published evidence schema digest.
Signetum writes only a Skill folder outside any Git work tree and its own guard entries in a host's user hook configuration; it never edits a project.
The Skill directory receives no generated runtime files.
No plugin manifest, marketplace or release pin.
revision.summary: One standard Skill folder is the distribution; an optional install command places it and registers the guard hook in a host's own configuration. The engine environment lives outside it.

boundaries: The guard applies in Git work trees whose root holds signetum.toml and allows every other command.
A guard that cannot run allows the command.
A missing guard yields guidance, never a refusal.
revision.summary: An optional PreToolUse hook refuses commands that lose work or bypass protocol operations in repositories that adopted Signetum.

transaction.reason: Apply the approved Skill distribution decisions.
